context_requirements: Concentrations of 10 µM exceed typical TCA plasma levels; response likely reflects off-target lysosomotropic/autophagic and HDAC-inhibitory effects rather than monoamine transporter blockade.
Cell lines must be actively proliferating and not fully growth-arrested for antiproliferative/autophagic transcriptional signatures to appear.
Intact apoptotic machinery (caspase-3, p75NTR/TrKA balance) may be required for the strongest responses.
PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling active (e.g., PTEN-null or PI3K-mutant lines) may enhance autophagic/DDIT4/TRIB3 responses.
falsifiers: No change in CDKN1A, SQSTM1, or proliferation genes at 24 h in any of the nine lines.
Strong, uniform upregulation of interferon or heat-shock programs at 6 h, which would suggest a different mechanism.
Clear induction of canonical monoamine-transporter-dependent transcriptional signatures at 6 h, which is not expected in these non-neuronal lines.
Absence of any antiproliferative or autophagic signature at 24 h despite 10 µM exposure.

evidence.supports: Imipramine inhibits PI3K/Akt/mTOR and induces autophagic cell death in glioma cells.
Amitriptyline inhibits HDACs, reduces cyclin D2, induces p21/p27, and causes G0/G1 arrest and apoptosis in myeloma cells.
Amitriptyline is cytotoxic to leiomyosarcoma cells via p75NTR-dependent apoptosis and AKT downregulation.
Nortriptyline inhibits myeloma cell growth, causes G2/M arrest and apoptosis.
Chronic desipramine alters hippocampal transcriptome in mice, showing TCA-responsive gene programs in vivo.
